headline: US Equities Rally on Iran De-escalation; Palantir, Onsemi Boost Tech
summary: US equities advanced as Middle East geopolitical tensions eased, driving oil prices lower. Strong earnings reports from Palantir and Onsemi provided a boost to the technology sector. The Bank of Japan maintained its policy rate, while the US Treasury increased its third-quarter borrowing estimate to $739 billion.

bullets.lead: Middle East tensions eased as diplomatic talks with Iran are set to begin.

segments.text: Trump reportedly called off a strike on Iran, with negotiations expected to commence, reducing geopolitical risks and contributing to a broader market overhang clearing.
Oil prices plummeted as investors digested the pause in Iran war fighting, leading to a rally in US stocks.

bullets.lead: Google is reportedly diversifying its AI chip packaging partners.

segments.text: Google is expanding orders for TPU AI server chips and has reportedly turned to Intel for EMIB packaging, as Nvidia has pre-booked over 50% of TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging capacity.

bullets.lead: TSMC is accelerating its advanced process capacity ramp-up.

segments.text: TSMC is reportedly ramping up its 3nm capacity to 180,000 wafer starts per month by early Q4, ahead of schedule, and its 2nm capacity to 100,000 wpm by year-end.

bullets.lead: NXP Semiconductors is in talks to acquire Ambarella.

segments.text: NXP Semiconductors is reportedly negotiating to acquire U.S. video/camera chip designer Ambarella, aiming to leverage its camera technology for self-driving car applications.

bullets.lead: South Korea's semiconductor exports saw significant growth.

segments.text: South Korea's semiconductor exports soared 179% year-on-year in July, reaching $41 billion, driven by rising global memory chip prices and strong shipments to China and the US.

bullets.lead: A severe shortage of Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates is impacting the industry.

segments.text: The CEO of Lumentum warned that the InP substrate shortage will be worse than memory, coinciding with AXT's $87 million deposit to reserve substrate capacity through 2031.

bullets.lead: Hyperscalers are increasing investments in AI infrastructure.

segments.text: Japan's NTT Data is investing 1.5 trillion yen in AI data centers, while Amazon is deepening its ties with OpenAI through a $50 billion AWS expansion.

x_themes.summary: Lumentum's CEO warned that the InP substrate shortage will be worse than memory, coinciding with AXT's filing of an $87M deposit to reserve substrate capacity through 2031, indicating extreme tightness in the market.

x_themes.topic: Market volatility and Leopold's leverage wipeout
x_themes.summary: The market experienced extreme volatility during an FOMC week, with Citadel reportedly profiting from a leveraged position after a surprise rate hold, while a trader named Leopold faced a leverage wipeout.
Trump reportedly called off a strike on Iran, with talks set to begin, easing geopolitical tensions and contributing to a broader market clearing of overhangs.

x_themes.topic: AAOI's InP laser fab expansion for 800G/1.6T transceivers
x_themes.summary: AAOI, as a vertically integrated transceiver maker with its own InP laser fab, is expanding capacity in Texas to meet pre-sold demand for 800G/1.6T transceivers, addressing the current InP laser shortage and providing a strategic U.S. supply for hyperscalers.

x_themes.topic: Samsung operating profit forecasts and LTA terms
x_themes.summary: Nomura significantly raised its operating profit forecasts for Samsung Electronics for the next three years, projecting substantial increases in FCF and shareholder return yields, with LTAs structured on supplier-friendly terms.

x_themes.topic: Record retail selling in Technology sector
x_themes.summary: Retail investors engaged in record-breaking selling in the Technology sector, with more notional value sold this week than any other since January 2019, exceeding the previous record by over 80%.

x_themes.topic: NXP in talks to acquire Ambarella
x_themes.summary: NXP Semiconductors is reportedly in talks to acquire U.S. video/camera chip designer Ambarella, aiming to leverage its camera technology for self-driving car applications.

x_themes.topic: Targeting of refined product and logistics assets
x_themes.summary: Aggressors are reportedly targeting refined product and logistics assets, rather than crude-related assets, potentially to limit political blowback, with drone warfare evolving.

x_themes.topic: Google's Intel EMIB use due to TSMC CoWoS constraints
x_themes.summary: Google is reportedly expanding orders for TPU AI server chips and has turned to Intel for EMIB packaging, as Nvidia has pre-booked over 50% of TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging capacity for the next three years.

TSMC is reportedly ramping up advanced process capacity, with 3nm expected to reach 180,000 wafer starts per month by early Q4 (ahead of schedule) and 2nm at 100,000 wpm by year-end, as clients like Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom vie for capacity.

x_themes.topic: Google Cloud supply constraints and rising CapEx
x_themes.summary: Google remains supply-constrained and anticipates significant CapEx increases in 2027, with spending focused on servers, data centers, and networking infrastructure to meet demand.

x_themes.topic: Chinese AI models' reliance on NVIDIA GPUs
x_themes.summary: Chinese AI model competition, exemplified by Moonshot's reported access to 20,000 NVIDIA GPUs via Alibaba, demonstrates the continued critical importance of large-scale NVIDIA compute infrastructure for even highly efficient Chinese models.

x_themes.topic: South Korea's soaring semiconductor exports in July
x_themes.summary: South Korea's semiconductor exports soared 179% year-on-year in July to $41 billion, driven by rising global memory chip prices and strong shipments to China and the US.

x_themes.topic: Microsoft Copilot progress and Azure CapEx ROI
x_themes.summary: Microsoft's Copilot progress exceeded expectations, and Azure shows an optimistic outlook with accelerated growth, improved CapEx ROI by hosting open-source models, and the ability to increase CapEx while remaining FCF-positive.
